surfaces.part: sand shore strip at top of tile

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain autotile: a 2-row sand strip across the top (rows 0-1, full 16px width) over a water fill (rows 2-15). The silhouette is 16 wide on every row. The water has only minor ripple pixels and a single highlight near row 12. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face, so it reads as a flat top-down terrain tile, not a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a single small swatch, far smaller than a 4x3 ground patch (64x48 source px). It is mostly one flat dark fill with a thin lighter strip along the top edge and a few specks, so about 3 readable shading steps against the references' 5 or more. The measured 38% near-flat coverage is far above both references (0%). The 11 visible tones per tile look inflated by the edge strip and specks, because the interior shows no grain, tufts or per-pixel variation. The grass reference has clumps and tufts, and the paving reference has shaded stones with highlights. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so this is not a black sticker outline. Even so, the piece reads as a flat fill with a border and has no texture. It would look thinner and flatter than the references, and the patch is incomplete for a 4x3 mask.
